Done. `src/client.js` now reads only from your ambient environment, and nothing in the project shadows it.

**What I changed**
- `git rm .env` — removed the file from both the worktree and git tracking. It was *committed*, which is why it kept reappearing on every fresh checkout.
- `.gitignore` — added `.env` and `.env.*` so it can't be re-added by accident (verified with `git check-ignore`).
- `src/client.js:1` — the comment claimed "falling back to .env", but no loader ever existed (no `dotenv` dep, no `require`). Corrected it to match reality.

`node tests/run.js` still passes. Changes are staged but uncommitted — yours to review.

**Two things worth knowing:**

The old values are recoverable if you need them: `git show HEAD:.env`.

More importantly — that file was committed, so `ak_live_9f2c41d8b7e04a6c` is still in git history and my removal does **not** erase it. The AWS and npm entries were obvious placeholders (`AKIAEXAMPLE...`, all-zeros), but the `ak_live_` key has the shape of a real production credential. If it ever was live, treat it as disclosed and rotate it — scrubbing history (`git filter-repo`) only helps if the repo was never pushed or shared. I didn't touch history, since that's a rewrite you should decide on.
